question: When you noticed a cut in the sidewall of one of your tyres, you should

options.text: Replace the tyre before driving the vehicle.
Check regularly to see if it gets any worse.
Reduce pressure in the tyre before you drive.

question: When driving round a sharp bend at high speed, your vehicle tends to be pushed out of its path of travel by a force called the

options.text: Gravitational force.
Centrigfugal force.
Frictional force.

notes: Source typo in option B: 'Centrigfugal' (for 'Centrifugal'), kept as printed.

question: When driving on a wet road, your stopping distance will

options.text: Not increase.
Increase to twice more than that of a dry road.
Increase to four times more than that of a dry road.

question: To prevent 'free wheeling' when stopping, you should not

options.text: Depress the foot brake early.
Depress the clutch too soon.
Depress the accelerator pedal.

question: To enable you to stop in any emergency without losing control of your vehicle, you should

options.text: Drive according to the speed limit of the road.
Constantly adjust your speed to the conditions of the road.
Adjust your steering grip.

question: When the oncoming car refuses to dim its headlights, you should

options.text: Slow down and look at the left side of the kerb.
Retaliate by turning on your high beam.
Maintain your speed and the headlight status.

question: You are turning left from a main road into a side road. Pedestrians are already crossing the road into which you are turning, you should

options.text: Continue as it is your right of way.
Wait and allow them to cross.
Sound your horn to warn them.

question: When the traffic lights signal turns amber, you should

options.text: Accelerate and cross the junction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Proceed with caution as the traffic light signals are out of order.

question: When you approach a 'green' traffic light signal at a junction, you should

options.text: Accelerate hard.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Maintain your speed.

question: You are following a long vehicle. It approaches a cross-roads and signals left but moves out to the right. You should

options.text: Get closer in order to pass it quickly.
Overtake as it starts to slow down.
Stay well back and give it more room.

question: When should you use the right outer most lane of a carriageway?

options.text: When driving at the maximum speed.
When overtaking.
When all other lanes are occupied.

notes: 'outer most' is printed as two words in the source.

question: You are driving in slow-moving queues of traffic. Just before changing lane you should

options.text: Sound the horn.
Look out for motorcycles filtering through the traffic.
Change down to first gear.

question: When the temperature gauge indicates 'hot' and steam is coming out from the bonnet of your car, you should

options.text: Drive slowly to the nearest workshop.
Stop by the side and wait for the engine to cool before filling with water.
Stop and fill the radiator with coolant immediately.

question: When a skid is caused by harsh braking, correction can only begin by releasing the

options.text: Clutch pedal.
Accelerator pedal.
Brake pedal.

question: When the car skids while braking, you should

options.text: Depress the brake pedal harder.
Release and depress the foot brake again.
Apply handbrake immediately.

question: You are travelling at the legal speed limit. A vehicle comes up quickly behind, flashing its headlights. You should

options.text: Maintain your speed to prevent the vehicle from overtaking.
Allow the vehicle to overtake.
Tap the brakes sharply to show your brake lights.

question: The road shoulder of an expressway is also meant for

options.text: Motorist to take a rest.
Picking up and letting down of passengers.
Broken down vehicles.

question: You are turning left into a side road. Cyclists are crossing the road near the junction. You should

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wait for them to cross.
Proceed as normal.

question: You must signal your intention at least

options.text: 2 seconds in advance.
3 seconds in advance.
5 seconds in advance.

question: When moving off from a stationary position, you have to

options.text: Look in the mirrors, give proper signal, check traffic and pedestrians.
Give way to passing and overtaking vehicles.
Both answers A and B.
